speaker: Doctor
text: Based on your history of being a nulliparous woman with a large ovarian mass, normal CA-125, and significant shortness of breath, do you notice the breathlessness worsening specifically when you lie flat (orthopnea) or if it improves when you sit up? speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, night sweats, chest pain, or swelling in the legs. She has not noticed any changes in bowel or urinary habits.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Ovarian Fibroma with Meigs Syndrome (Ovarian Fibroma, Ascites, Pleural Effusion).

The combination of a large benign-appearing ovarian mass, ascites (increased abdominal girth), and shortness of breath (likely due to pleural effusion) with a normal CA-125 strongly suggests Meigs syndrome. We need to confirm the presence of the pleural effusion and rule out malignancy before confirming this diagnosis.
